1jkibwu: Tener que, hay que, and necesitar
15me188: **Tener que + infinitive** expresses an obligation of a specific person. The verb _tener_ changes with the person: **Tengo que limpiar el baño. ¿Tienes que trabajar el sábado? Mis hermanos tienen que estudiar.**
ic29wi: **Hay que + infinitive** expresses a general obligation, for everyone, without saying who. _Hay que_ never changes and has no subject: **En esta casa hay que sacar la basura los martes. Hay que pedir cita para renovar el pasaporte.**
1uza9jf: **Necesitar** expresses need. It goes with an infinitive or a noun, without a preposition: **Necesito comprar pan. Necesitamos una escoba nueva.**
5mcy6m: The three forms combine with the time markers you already know: **Mañana tengo que ir al banco. Esta semana hay que limpiar la terraza.**
18xxuw8: Ask yourself: is it a rule for everyone (_en esta casa…_, _en el trabajo…_)? → **hay que**. Is it my obligation or yours? → **tengo que / tienes que**.
118j9dy: Three ways of talking about obligations
1l6rfz: The obligation is **tener que** + infinitive: without _que_ it doesn't work.
4r28d6: After _hay que_ there is always the **infinitive**.
101nlkr: _Hay que_ has no subject. For a specific person: **tengo que**.
1avk3e4: _Necesitar_ goes directly with the infinitive, without _de_.
h44nnp: Lo, la, los, las: not repeating
1sgbijw: When a thing is already in the conversation, we don't repeat it: we use **lo, la, los, las**. The pronoun agrees with the word it replaces: **el pan → lo**, **la basura → la**, **los platos → los**, **las plantas → las**.
1s83shp: With a conjugated verb, the pronoun goes **before** the verb: **—¿Quién compra el pan? —Lo compro yo. —¿Y las plantas? —Las riego yo.**
66if3p: With an infinitive (after _tener que_, _ir a_, _hay que_…), you have two options: **before the conjugated verb** or **attached to the end of the infinitive**: **La tengo que limpiar** = **Tengo que limpiarla**. **Los voy a lavar** = **Voy a lavarlos.** Both are correct and common.
17p4eqt: With _hay que_ there is only one option: attached to the infinitive. **¿La cocina? Hay que limpiarla.**
7g6cey: When you attach the pronoun to the infinitive, the stress stays in the same place: _lim**piar**lo, com**prar**la_. It doesn't need an accent mark.
1wzu3ud: With a conjugated verb, the pronoun goes **before**.
1n0trut: The pronoun doesn't go between _que_ and the infinitive: **lo tengo que limpiar** or **tengo que limpiarlo**.
1ki8zo7: When the direct object is a specific **person**, we put **a** in front: **Llamo a mi madre. Visito a mis abuelos. Ayudo a Carmen con la mudanza.** With things, no: **Llamo un taxi. Visito el museo.**
18jnnk8: Remember the contraction: **a + el = al**. **Llamo al plomero** (Latin America) / **al fontanero** (Spain).
9o6o1o: To replace a person we also use **lo, la, los, las**: **—¿Ves a Diego hoy? —Sí, lo veo en la cena. —¿Y a las niñas? —Las llevo yo al colegio.**
coauhk: In Spain many people use **le** for a man: _A Diego le veo mañana_. It's normal to hear it; you can use **lo**, which is understood everywhere.
dpxed9: _Mi abuela_ is a specific person: it needs **a**.
l635jd: A taxi is a thing (a service): without **a**.
1yqarrx: To share out tasks, ask **¿Quién…?** and answer with the pronoun and the subject at the end: **—¿Quién hace la cena? —La hago yo.** Putting _yo_ at the end is very natural when you offer.
sy9gh: To talk about turns, use **tocar**: **Hoy me toca a mí. ¿A quién le toca sacar la basura? Te toca a ti.** It's the same in Spain and in Latin America.
1nc9sc6: To give tasks to a group, remember: in Spain **vosotros tenéis que…**; in Latin America **ustedes tienen que…**. To ask politely: **¿Puedes lavar los platos?** (tú) / **¿Puede usted…?** (usted).

18qv698: Consonant clusters: tr, pr, pl, bl, cr, gr
q2v1ww: Many Spanish words have two consonants together before the vowel: **tr**es, **pl**ato, ha**bl**ar, o**tr**o, **gr**ande, **cr**ema, **pr**imo. The two consonants go **in the same syllable**: o-**tro**, ha-**blar**, li-**bro**.
1o7p7g1: The golden rule: **don't add a vowel** in the middle. _Tres_ has one syllable, not two ("te-res"). _Plato_ has two, not three ("pe-la-to").
3qhyyr: The **r** inside the cluster is always **single**, the short r of _pero_: a single quick tap of the tongue. Don't make the strong rr of _perro_ in _tres_ or _otro_.
1nan7ii: The **l** of the cluster is clear, with the tip of the tongue behind the upper teeth: **pl**aya, **bl**anco, **cl**ase.
1b1avzy: Variation: in Chile and in parts of Costa Rica and the Andes, the **tr** cluster sometimes sounds almost like **ch**: _otro_ can sound similar to "ocho." It's a normal variant; you can use the general tr.
yyq4d9: When dividing syllables, the cluster is never broken: _o-tro_, _ha-blar_, _ne-gro_, _li-bro_. That's why, if a word doesn't fit at the end of the line, it is cut like this: _ha-_ / _blar_.
isj5ix: **tr**es, **pr**ar, **pl**antas: a single tap of the tongue for the r, with no extra vowel.
1x2reqq: **pr**imo, **tr**abaja, **pr**onto: the r is short, as in _pero_.
bpg1mq: es-**cri**-bir, ha-**blar**, **gru**-po: the two consonants begin the syllable.
9unv85: O-**tro**, **tra**-po, **blan**-co. Start slowly and speed up without adding vowels.
